findings.input_id: GitHub CodeQL alert 122 / py/path-injection / Python analysis 2101152167
findings.title: Reported application_id path injection in the manual authentication path validator

normalized_input.claimed_source: Untrusted application_id path parameter at apps/api/manual_auth.py:119
normalized_input.claimed_sink: Path.is_symlink() at services/applications/manual_auth.py:320, reached through configured application/browser-profile paths
normalized_input.claimed_control: The scanner tracks user influence into a filesystem path; its alert does not establish that the existing identifier and containment controls can be bypassed
normalized_input.affected_version_or_path: Reported main e56f9022185c209465f53cf89bbf7818c60efe8a; local target 43cad34752c5b2f281ce94277bd0bf5af04506e8 has the identical complete tree cd799ec69c2afc2190b0a98c20ba299f7ade50ae
preconditions: The manual-auth HTTP route is called in an ACTIVE FIXTURE workspace for a matching profile/application, MOCK target, AUTH_REQUIRED application and current attempt.
The caller supplies an application_id that survives service-level validation before path construction.
normalized_input.impact: Claimed access to unexpected filesystem resources through a user-influenced path; no exploit or arbitrary file-content access was supplied

affected_locations.label: entrypoint
affected_locations.detail: HTTP application_id source; FIXTURE, profile/application identity, MOCK target, AUTH_REQUIRED application and current-attempt checks precede dispatch.

affected_locations.label: dispatch
affected_locations.detail: Windows dispatches through the isolated helper; non-Windows dispatches through mock_adapter.

affected_locations.label: identifier controls
affected_locations.detail: Anchored lowercase hexadecimal identifier of exactly 64 characters and a basename-equality check precede every reported application-root construction; attempt IDs are32 hexadecimal characters.

affected_locations.label: reported sink and containment
affected_locations.detail: The reported sink checks symlinks/junctions, fails closed on path exceptions, and is used before/after canonicalization with separator-terminated containment checks.

affected_locations.label: Windows caller
affected_locations.detail: The operation binding is checked, _resolve_auth_attempt applies the common identifier validation, and the validated ID enters a bounded private child payload.

affected_locations.label: Windows child
affected_locations.detail: The child validates a bounded JSON object and separator-free identifier, requires an absolute configured root, checks aliases and exact application-parent/name plus browser-profile containment before use.

affected_locations.label: non-Windows caller
affected_locations.detail: Forwards to open_manual_auth_window, which independently repeats the identifier validation before _resolve_auth_attempt.

affected_locations.label: profile selection
affected_locations.detail: Profile labels have a narrow separator-free grammar and Windows reserved-name rejection; bounded manifest parsing and alias checks preserve application confinement. The reported resolver uses initialize=False.

affected_locations.label: configuration provenance
affected_locations.detail: The API factory closes over output_dir supplied by server startup from MJOBS_OUTPUT_DIR; the reported request does not supply that filesystem root.

reachable_path: An HTTP caller supplies application_id to the FIXTURE-only manual-auth route; the API checks the persisted application/profile, target and current attempt.
On Windows, the isolated helper validates the operation binding and calls _resolve_auth_attempt; on other platforms, mock_adapter calls open_manual_auth_window, which calls the same resolver.
Before joining paths, the resolver rejects any application_id that is not exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, rejects basename changes, and validates the 32-character hexadecimal attempt ID.
The configured root receives only the validated application path component; browser profile selection returns a separately validated, application-confined path.
The selected SARIF sink is the symlink/junction check itself. Canonicalization and repeated alias/containment checks follow it before a profile can be returned.
The Windows child and optional diagnostic-root handling apply additional validation; no later transformation of the accepted application ID restores separators or traversal syntax.

boundary_assessment.policy_basis: Root SECURITY.md:3,5,11 identifies a developer preview, requires preserving open findings and private handling of actual vulnerabilities, and points to supported installation/automation boundaries. No nearer SECURITY.md exists under apps/api or services/applications. docs/INSTALLATION.md:3,15,23,31 supports the fictional FIXTURE workflow. The verdict evaluates that supported alternate path; it does not rely solely on PERSONAL mode denying the route.

exploitability_stack_rank.rationale: Positive identifier and containment controls defeat the reported HTTP application_id traversal across the traced supported callers.

evidence: The actual current-main CodeQL instance and Python SARIF analysis 2101152167 were retrieved. The selected result contains source-to-sink flows from apps/api/manual_auth.py:119 into manual_auth.py:320 through both platform dispatch paths.
The source and local revisions differ in commit identity but have exactly the same complete tree cd799ec69c2afc2190b0a98c20ba299f7ade50ae. The read-only checkout remained clean.
manual_auth.py blob 22546aea6c2246aff31acce447b0263b000b5384 and API blob a2a48f0dde0379df0aa92d501cf781dbcb637c33 were inspected with both the lexical identifier guards and downstream consumers.

Manual policy resolution checked root and each applicable ancestor for API, service, isolated child, profile helper and adapter files. Shared skill resolver/assessment references were unavailable in this environment, as recorded in this run's earlier triage; the explicit nearest-policy checks are retained.
counterevidence: The application ID remains untrusted, but the effective allowlist of 64 hexadecimal characters excludes slashes, backslashes, dots, drive syntax, percent escapes and other path-control characters before filesystem path construction. A matching persisted record does not bypass this service-level check.
The sink at line 320 is a defensive metadata check, not an unguarded file-content read/write. It rejects aliases and exceptions.
Both actual platform paths apply the common guard. The Windows child additionally validates its bounded payload and confines the resolved application/profile paths.
The output root is startup configuration captured by the router, rather than a field on the reported HTTP request; profile selection values are constrained independently.
proof_gaps: This is static evidence only: no tests, browser launch, application execution, PoC or runtime exploit validation was performed.

The verdict is limited to alert 122's HTTP application_id traversal claim. A separate actor able to modify the server process environment or race filesystem objects, and the other 48 open alerts, are not assessed here.
findings.recommended_next_step: Retain this narrow evidence for maintainer disposition of alert 122. No source change or broad scanner suppression is justified for the reported application_id path. The alert remains open and no acceptance status is promoted.
